name: Julie Byrne
label: Ghostly International
lede: Julie Byrne learned guitar at seventeen on her father's instrument and later patrolled Central Park as a ranger. Six years after Not Even Happiness, The Greater Wings won Pitchfork's Best New Music and landed at No. 21 on its 2023 year-end list.

eras.title: Her father's guitar
eras.text: Born in Buffalo, Byrne took up her father's guitar as a teenager and left home at eighteen. Half a dozen cities later, her first songs went out on cassette.

years.src: Wikipedia: Julie Byrne · Wikipedia: The Greater Wings
years.h: Her father can't play anymore, so Byrne learns his guitar
years.p: He played fingerstyle until complications from multiple sclerosis meant he couldn't. Byrne, born in Buffalo in 1990, learned at seventeen on his instrument.
years.xp:
According to Wikipedia, Byrne has described learning his guitar as "an offering to him", a way to honor a craft he could no longer practice.

Her later records keep that fingerstyle core, even as The Greater Wings adds synthesizer, harp and strings.

years.src: Wikipedia: Julie Byrne · Stereogum: Q&A: Julie Byrne
years.h: Six cities after Buffalo, Byrne lands in New York
years.p: Wikipedia lists Pittsburgh, Northampton, Chicago, Lawrence, Seattle and New Orleans before she settles in New York.
years.xp: Stereogum quotes her on the other side of that restlessness, years later: "I'm not willing to live the way that I did before." By then she was trying to stay put.

eras.title: Cassettes, a park, a breakthrough
eras.text: Two cassettes became a debut. A job in Central Park gave her a second life, and a record made in her childhood home carried her name past indie circles.

years.cap: Julie Byrne at a house show in Arcata, California, March 2014.
years.src: Stereogum: Q&A: Julie Byrne · Wikipedia: Julie Byrne
years.h: Two cassettes become Rooms with Walls and Windows
years.p: The debut compiles her self-titled tape from 2012 and You Would Love It Here from 2013, both cassette-only until then.
years.xp: Stereogum's Q&A says the tapes were recorded live in Chicago in a show space.

years.cap: Julie Byrne at Park Church Co-Op, Brooklyn.
years.src: Wikipedia: Julie Byrne · Stereogum: Q&A: Julie Byrne
years.h: By day, Byrne is a Central Park ranger
years.p: She had studied environmental science, and Wikipedia quotes her calling the park a sanctuary for New Yorkers and for wildlife.
years.xp: Stereogum reports the job answered her need for green space while living in New York City.

years.cap: Julie Byrne at Haldern Pop Festival, Germany, August 11, 2017.
years.src: Wikipedia: Not Even Happiness · Stereogum: Q&A: Julie Byrne
yt: Full session at Paste Studios, New York, 2017
years.h: Not Even Happiness comes out twice, two weeks apart
years.p: Basin Rock released it in the UK on January 13 and Ba Da Bing in the US on January 27. Pitchfork gave it 8.3.
years.xp:
Nine songs, 32 minutes. Eric Littmann produced, recorded and mixed it in Buffalo, and Stereogum places the sessions at Byrne's childhood home. Jake Falby's string arrangements were done at a cabin in Holderness, New Hampshire. Michele Finkelstein played flute, Chris Masullo guitar and Johanna Warren sang backing vocals.

Wikipedia lists a Metacritic score of 82 from 22 critics, and year-end spots at Spin (No. 9), Stereogum (No. 20) and Paste (No. 27).

years.cap: Julie Byrne at the Sea Change festival, St Mary's church, Totnes, England, August 26, 2017.
years.h: A heavy night in Boulder becomes "Natural Blue"
years.p: Byrne wrote the song before a 10-hour drive to Kansas, in the middle of a 40-day tour, she told Stereogum.
years.xp: She described a tour with almost no rest. The song is that life written down as it happened.

eras.title: Six years, and a loss in the middle
eras.text: Byrne began the follow-up with Eric Littmann in Chicago. A pandemic interrupted it, then his death stopped it, and Alex Somers helped her finish.

years.cap: Julie Byrne at The Wonder Inn, Manchester.
years.src: Wikipedia: The Greater Wings · Loud and Quiet: Julie Byrne · 13th Floor: Julie Byrne Remains On The Edge Of Mystery
years.h: The Greater Wings begins in Eric Littmann's Chicago home studio
years.p: Wikipedia dates the first recording to 2018, with Byrne and Littmann working in the studio he kept there.
years.xp:
Other interviews put the restart at 2019 or early 2020, so the start date is loose. Byrne told Loud and Quiet she began writing the first chords in 2017, right after Not Even Happiness.

She said of the long gap: "The songs in and of themselves are stories that needed to be lived out and that took time."

years.src: Wikipedia: The Greater Wings · Paste: How Julie Byrne Found New Heights
years.h: Eric Littmann, Byrne's partner and producer, dies in 2021
years.p: Byrne on what made working with Littmann so rich. Per Wikipedia, the sessions for The Greater Wings stopped.
years.xp:
The full quote: "It wasn't even his vision or technical skill or artistry that made the collaboration so rich and singular, it was his love and care."

Paste describes him as a University of Chicago lab manager who co-produced with a portable suitcase recording setup. Sources do not state a cause of death.

years.src: 13th Floor: Julie Byrne Remains On The Edge Of Mystery · Paste: How Julie Byrne Found New Heights · Wikipedia: The Greater Wings
years.h: Alex Somers steps in, and the Catskills finish the record
years.p: Somers helps Byrne complete it with collaborators she already trusted.
years.xp:
13th Floor reports production resumed in early 2022 in the Catskills. Jake Falby, who arranged strings on Not Even Happiness, returned for violin, guitar, piano and synth sessions in Los Angeles, according to Paste.

Byrne on Somers: "Being a producer is such an art... it's also a grace of relationship."

eras.title: Everywhere on the year-end lists
eras.text: After six years, three singles and a record about grief, Byrne turned up on critics' lists across the board.

years.h: Six years on, "Summer Glass" is the first word on The Greater Wings
years.p: The lead single arrives April 24, ahead of the album on Ghostly International.

years.src: Paste: Listen to Julie Byrne's New Single Moonless · 13th Floor: Julie Byrne Remains On The Edge Of Mystery
years.h: At a Portuguese residency, Byrne writes "Moonless" at the piano
years.p: It was her first song written on piano, made during an artist residency in Culatra, and she calls it a breakup song.
years.xp:
Paste says she wrote it walking the dunes on the ocean side of Culatra, with dock noises, tidal-flat smells and a coast in constant erosion on her mind.

13th Floor adds that she began piano lessons at 28.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Greater Wings · Metacritic: The Greater Wings · Pitchfork on X: Julie Byrne's The Greater Wings is named Best New Music
yt: A Take Away Show, West Hurley, NY, July 2023
years.h: Pitchfork gives The Greater Wings 8.5 and Best New Music
years.p: Ghostly released the ten-song album on July 7. Metacritic lists 91 from 13 critics.
years.xp:
Pitchfork's 8.5 comes from Wikipedia's reception table. The album was recorded across 2018, 2021 and 2022 in Chicago, Buffalo and Los Angeles, with Jake Falby, Eric Littmann and Alex Somers credited as producers. It adds synthesizer, harp and strings to her guitar.

The Guardian gave it 5/5 and AllMusic 4.5/5. Wikipedia reports it as her first US chart appearance, at No. 90 on Top Current Album Sales.

years.src: Wikipedia: Julie Byrne with Laugh Cry Laugh
years.h: Byrne and Laugh Cry Laugh cover Jackson Browne on a four-song EP
years.p: The 11-minute EP came out on Ghostly. Paste ranked it the 24th best EP of 2023.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists Emily Fontana on bass and Taryn Blake Miller on recording and engineering.

years.h: By December, Pitchfork has The Greater Wings at No. 21
years.p: Paste has it at No. 6, Uncut at No. 9 and Mojo at No. 10.
years.xp: Per Wikipedia, the album was also nominated for Best Folk Record at the 2024 Libera Awards.
